Module np.cincuentazo
Package np.cincuentazo.model

Class GameState

java.lang.Object
np.cincuentazo.model.GameState
public class GameState extends Object
Holds the complete, authoritative state of a Cincuentazo game session.

Single source of truth

Every piece of information the controller or the view needs about the ongoing game lives here: the deck, the table cards, the table sum, the player list, and whose turn it is. Neither the controller nor the view store game data independently â€” they always read from and write to this object.

Separation of concerns

GameState is a data model, not a rules engine. It exposes mutation methods (playCard(np.cincuentazo.model.Card), advanceTurn()) but enforces no game rules internally. Rule enforcement (e.g., "is this card legal?", "is the game over?") is the responsibility of the controller, which reads state, checks rules, then calls the appropriate mutation.

Table cards structure

A Stack is used for table cards because the game always interacts with the top card: the last played card is visible on top, and when recycling cards back to the deck, the top card stays while everything below goes to the deck. Stack's peek() and pop() map naturally to these operations.

  • Constructor Details

    • GameState

      public GameState(List<Player> players)
      Creates a new game state for the given player list, using a freshly shuffled deck. The first card is dealt to the table to start the sum. Setup sequence
      1. Store players (human at index 0, machines at 1-3).
      2. Deal 4 cards to each player (face up for human, face down for machines).
      3. Draw one card and place it face up on the table to seed the sum.
      4. Set currentTurnIndex = 0 so the human goes first.
      Parameters:
      players - ordered list of players; index 0 must be the human player; must have 2â€“4 elements
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if players is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the player count is outside [2, 4]

  • Method Details

    • advanceTurn

      public void advanceTurn()
      Advances currentTurnIndex to the next alive player, wrapping around the list circularly.

      This method assumes the game is not over â€” the caller must check isGameOver() before calling this, otherwise it would loop forever looking for a second alive player that does not exist.

    • playCard

      public void playCard(Card card)
      Places a card on the table and updates the table sum.

      The card is flipped face up (it becomes visible to all), pushed onto the table stack, and its value is added to the running sum.

      Pre-condition: the controller must have validated that playing this card is legal before calling this method.

      Parameters:
      card - the card just played by the current player; must not be null

    • refillDeckIfNeeded

      public boolean refillDeckIfNeeded()
      Checks whether the deck is empty and, if so, refills it from the table cards (all except the top card).

      This must be called before drawing a replacement card at the end of a player's turn. If the deck is not empty, this is a no-op.

      Returns:
      true if a refill was performed, false if the deck had cards and no refill was needed

    • dealCardToPlayer

      public void dealCardToPlayer(Player player)
      Draws one card from the deck and gives it to the specified player. Call refillDeckIfNeeded() first if the deck might be empty.
      Parameters:
      player - the player who receives the drawn card; must not be null

    • eliminatedCurrentPlayer

      public void eliminatedCurrentPlayer()
      Eliminates the current player: marks them as out, removes their hand cards, and sends those cards to the bottom of the deck.

      Called when the current player has no playable card on their turn.

    • isGameOver

      public boolean isGameOver()
      Returns true if only one player remains alive â€” that player is the winner.

      The controller calls this after every turn resolution (either after a successful play or after an elimination) to decide whether to continue or end the game.

      Returns:
      true when the game has a winner
